title: Indian Startups Raised $233 Million Last Week as Simple Energy's $180M Round Dominated
excerpt: Sixteen Indian startups raised $233.6 million in the week of Sept 28–Oct 2, per Inc42's tracker — but Simple Energy's $180 million Series C alone made up three-quarters of it.
body:
• Indian startups raised $233.6 million across 16 deals in the week of September 28–October 2, up 14.9% from the previous week's $203 million, according to Inc42's weekly tracker.
  • EV maker Simple Energy's $180 million Series C — led by the Dr. Arokiaswamy Velumani Family Office — accounted for roughly three-quarters of the week's entire funding.
  • Early-stage activity was lukewarm: seed and pre-seed rounds totaled just $3.3 million across four deals.
  • Alteria Capital was the week's most active investor with three deals; ecommerce led by deal count (4 deals) even as cleantech took the money.

Indian startup funding picked up in the first week of October, with startups raising $233.6 million across 16 deals in the week of September 28–October 2, according to Inc42's weekly funding tracker — a 14.9% increase in value over the previous week, even as the number of deals fell 23.8%.

One round ran the table

The week's headline was Simple Energy, the Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler maker, which closed a $180 million Series C led by the Dr. Arokiaswamy Velumani Family Office, with participation from the Haran Family Office, angel investor Amit Mishra, and co-founders Suhas Rajkumar and Ankit Gupta. (A second tracker, inshorts, pegged the same round at $182 million.) Alone, the round represented roughly 77% of the week's total — a reminder of how top-heavy Indian startup funding has become, with cleantech and mobility absorbing the largest checks.

"Proptech player Gravity raised $15 million from 3one4 Capital, Info Edge Ventures, Alteria Capital and Genesia Ventures."

Beyond the big round

The rest of the week was a spread of mid-sized bets. Proptech player Gravity raised $15 million from 3one4 Capital, Info Edge Ventures, Alteria Capital and Genesia Ventures. Fintech lender Seeds Fincap and agritech company Balwaan Krishi each raised $10.4 million Series B rounds, while edtech startup Arivihan closed a $10.2 million Series A from Accel and Prosus Ventures. Smaller rounds included EDT's $2.4 million pre-Series A and the Bangalore Watch Company's $1.4 million seed.

By sector, cleantech topped the money table; proptech came second; and ecommerce led on deal activity with four deals worth a combined $3.8 million. Seed and pre-seed funding stayed soft at $3.3 million across four deals — a sign that early-stage investors remain cautious even as growth-stage money flows.

The broader week

It was a busy week beyond the funding tally. Moneyview listed on the BSE at ₹55.6, a 64% premium over its ₹34 issue price. AceVector's ₹420 crore IPO was oversubscribed 4.93 times ahead of its October 5 debut. Tonbo Imaging received SEBI approval for its IPO, Ola Electric's board approved a ₹1,000 crore rights issue, and ITC completed its 100% acquisition of Yoga Bar's parent for ₹645 crore.

What's next

Weekly totals vary by methodology — inshorts tallied the same week at $411.46 million across 24 deals — but the direction is consistent: the festive-quarter pipeline is filling up, with Simple Energy's mega-round and a string of public-market debuts suggesting late-2026 could be the strongest funding stretch of the year. The watch item for founders: whether early-stage checks, still stuck at $3.3 million a week, recover in the coming months.
